description: Writes the editing guide for a film, scene by scene: what each shot is for, where to cut and why, which cutaway or insert covers which jump or crossed line, the sound to lay, and each open finding as a note about what to do in the edit. With a take log it also says which take stands for each shot and marks shots that have no usable take; without one it works from the plan alone. The tools take text only, never video or audio, and no AI model runs. Input: plan; optionally takes (a dpl.takes/1 log). Output: dpl.edit-guide/1, as JSON. We don't keep the plan or the take log. Needs an agent key from a Shoot Plan account, and is free up to 3 projects a month. A project is identified by the plan's work id and title; it counts when this tool first makes a finished document for it that month. shoot_plan_allowance says what is left. Over the limit it answers ALLOWANCE_REACHED: do not retry, a new key will not help, tell your human. A fair-use limit also applies: up to 20 finished-document calls for any one project and 60 for the account each month. To count projects we keep, against your account, a one-way fingerprint (hash) of the project's id and title, the month, how many finished documents were made and when, for 13 months after the end of that month. Plans up to 8 MB and 120 calls a minute (5,000 a day).

plan.description: The plan itself: a dpl.plan/1 JSON object (not text inside a string). Call shoot_plan_format for the schema links and an example.

takes.description: The take log: a dpl.takes/1 JSON object, {format, work_id, takes: [...]}. Each take has op_id, shot (the plan's shot id), kind and verdict; file names and timecodes are optional. A take log holds text about recordings: the tools take no video or audio.

name: shoot_plan_edit_guide
title: A guide for the editor, from the plan and the takes
